subject.title: Enhancement: Allow custom safe headers in fetch-guard cross-origin redirects

question: Should OpenClaw allow operator-configured custom headers to survive cross-origin fetch-guard redirects, and if yes must the permission be scoped by redirect destination origin rather than a global header-name allowlist?
rationale: The request changes a credential-forwarding boundary and adds public config surface, so automation cannot choose the acceptable trust model or guardrails.

options.title: Design scoped operator policy
options.body: Add the capability only with header-name validation, destination-origin scoping, documentation, and tests proving the default remains strict.

options.title: Keep strict stripping only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and keep custom credential-like headers blocked on all cross-origin redirects.

options.title: Add global header extension list
options.body: Implement the proposed header-name-only config, accepting the higher risk that an allowed header can be replayed to any redirect origin.

recommendation.title: Design scoped operator policy
recommendation.body: Add the capability only with header-name validation, destination-origin scoping, documentation, and tests proving the default remains strict.

likelyOwner.reason: The current strict custom-header behavior traces to steipete's security hardening commit, and the decision is about changing that trust boundary.
